chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abu al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, from Muhammad ibn Bishr al-Hamdani, who said:

I heard Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah say: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) related to me that on the Day of Resurrection, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be holding Allah's Waistband, we (the family of the Prophet) will be holding our Prophet's Waistband, and our Shi'ites will be holding our Waistband. I asked, 'O Commander of the Faithful, what is the Waistband?' He answered, 'Allah is greater than being characterized with a waistband or anything else. However, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) will be holding Allah's Affair, we (the family of Muhammad) will be holding our Prophet's Affair, and our Shi'ites will be holding our Affair.'

key_terms.آل مُحَمَّد: The Family of Muhammad; referring to the Ahl al-Bayt.
key_terms.أَمْر: Affair/Command; referring to divine authority or jurisdiction.
key_terms.حُجْزَة: Waistband; a metaphor for holding onto authority, command, or spiritual connection.
key_terms.شِيعَتُنَا: Our Shi'ites/Followers; referring to the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of holding the waistband (hujzah) on the Day of Resurrection in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Tawhid elucidates the metaphysical chain of authority (silsilah) on the Day of Resurrection, where 'holding the waistband' signifies grasping the divine command (amr). It establishes a hierarchical spiritual linkage: the Prophet Muhammad holds Allah's command, the Ahl al-Bayt hold the Prophet's, and the Shi'ah hold the Ahl al-Bayt's, thereby validating the Shi'ah's direct connection to divine guidance through their Imams. This concept underscores the Shia belief in the infallible transmission of religious authority and the esoteric role of the Imams as the living embodiment of the Prophet's legacy.
